summary: Pyramid Rock Light, established 1941 on the Mokapu Peninsula inside Marine Corps Base Hawaii at Kaneohe Bay; Coast Guard light with no public access.

structures.note: 15 ft (4.5 m) square concrete workhouse with the beacon on its roof, painted with black and white diagonal stripes (Rowlett; Lighthouse Friends)

access.note: On an active Marine Corps base; non-military visitors are not allowed access (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Established atop the natural feature on the northwest point of the Mokapu Peninsula (Lighthouse Friends); Rowlett gives station established 1941

First shown as an occulting white light (Oc W 4s) in the Society's historical list for 1971-1972, after the isophase entry for 1952-1956. The list's OCR prints no characteristic for 1957-1970, so the change itself is undated in the sources; the year is when the list first shows the occulting light.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett's undated entry gives an occulting white light every 4 s. The Society's historical list gives an isophase white light (Iso W 2s) for 1950 to 1956 and an occulting white light (Oc W 4s) for 1971 to 1985. The 2025 Light List entry 28675 gives Fl W 6s, which the facts record as current. The sources do not date the change from isophase to occulting.

notes_for_editor: 1) Builder, cost and 1941 construction details: none of the sources read names them. A Navy or Marine Corps history of NAS Kaneohe Bay would be the next place to look. 2) The 2025 Light List, Volume VI, entry 28675 (Pyramid Rock Light, 21-27-44.140N 157-45-48.780W, Fl W 6s, range 10, 'On post on concrete structure with black and white markings') is now footnoted as source 5 (npshistory copy of the same volume). Focal height 30.8 m is from Rowlett's focal plane 101 ft (31 m); the Light List prints no heights. 3) roster.py found no USLHS place for Pyramid Rock (no match by name and state), so no keeper roster. The station is automated per all sources. 4) One Chronicling America search for Hawaiian papers, 1939 to 1946, for 'Pyramid Rock' and 'light' returned no hits. 5) The HABS report is for the NAS Kaneohe administration building. It is used for the air-station attack detail only, not for the light. 6) Rowlett calls the feature a pyramidal rock; LighthouseFriends calls it a natural feature. 7) Station record agency is null; the proposed correction is in corrections. 8) The USLHS list's 1971-1972 entry is the first to show Oc W 4s; the OCR prints no characteristic for 1957-1970, so the change is undated. The event year 1971 means first shown in the list. 9) Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett are treated as copyrighted: paraphrased, with one short quotation each. 10) NRHP not checked (no NRHP number in the record). 11) No storms, wrecks or rescues found in sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 'northwest point' quotation (the source says 'northwestern') was altered in the draft and is now paraphrased; the isophase and occulting dates were corrected (Iso W 2s runs 1950 to 1956, not 1950-1951 only; Oc W 4s is listed from 1971, not only in the 1980s); the Light List characteristic and range are footnoted; the bay mouth is given in nautical miles with statute miles in brackets.
